findings.title: Live-looking payment gateway API key hardcoded in source
findings.note: Module-level constant holds an sk_live_-prefixed key (Stripe live-key shape) used directly as the Authorization bearer token for real refund POSTs, not under a test/fixture path.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled for gateway refund calls

evidence.quote:
def refund(self, order_id: str, amount_cents: int) -> bool:
        response = requests.post(
            f"{self.base}/refunds",
            json={"order": order_id, "amount": amount_cents},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", **CORS_HEADERS},
            verify=False,
        )

findings.note: verify=False is unconditional on every refund POST from Gateway, with no environment flag scoping it to a local/dev target; it applies to the same code path that moves real money.

findings.title: Access-Control-Allow-Origin wildcard sent as outbound request header
findings.note: Wildcard CORS header is merged into the client's outbound request headers to the gateway, not a server response; it has no browser-enforced effect here but signals a misunderstanding of the header's purpose and could be copy-pasted into a server response path later.

findings.title: SQL f-string interpolation of refund_id, nosec with no justification

evidence.quote:
def export_v1(refund_id: str, db: str = "refunds.db") -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    con = sqlite3.connect(db)
    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.execute(f"SELECT id, amount FROM refunds WHERE id = '{refund_id}'")  # nosec

findings.note: refund_id is a caller-supplied string interpolated directly into SQL text; no in-repo caller exists but the file's own TODO says it is kept for the still-running v1 reporting job, implying external invocation. The # nosec has no comment explaining why the injection risk is not real.

findings.title: subprocess shell=True with unsuppressed injection potential pattern

evidence.quote: subprocess.run("mail -s report finance@example.com", shell=True)  # noqa: S602

findings.note: Command string is fully hardcoded (no variable interpolation) so no current input reaches the shell, but shell=True is used with a lint suppression and no comment justifying it.

open_questions.question: fingerprint() uses md5 on order_id but has no callers anywhere in the repo; cannot determine whether it is intended for a security-sensitive purpose (identity/token) or a non-security dedup/cache key, which would make the weak hash a non-finding per the stated trap.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: api_key value is 'sk_test_placeholder_xxx_do_not_use', clearly a test fixture placeholder, not a real credential.

not_assessed: Whether the gateway.py api_key is an actually active/valid credential (cannot verify against Stripe or any service).
Whether export_v1 in legacy_export.py is actually invoked by an external v1 reporting job as its TODO comment implies, since no caller exists in this repository.
Exploitability of the SQL injection or shell command in production (no runtime/deployment context available).
